# KS-1220 - Wednesday's task for Ornith, VITEST, **TEST-ONLY MODE, MODIFY THE EXISTING TEST IN PLACE** (two hunks) (written 21:21 AEST on 2026-09-17)

file `Blockchain/Dev/services/auth/src/__tests__/ks839-a-wildcard-allow-list-grants-nothing.test.ts` (101 lines) was read whole; the
product file `Blockchain/Dev/services/auth/src/services/oauth.ts` was read at `:348-:360` (`validateScopes` and `parseScopeString`).
KS-1220 (0 comments) and the #1026 round-2 gate report (finding F-4, tamper row G-SECOND-REGEX) were read.

## THE MODE - read this twice

TEST-ONLY, MODIFY IN PLACE. Your diff contains EXACTLY ONE file: the EXISTING test file
`Blockchain/Dev/services/auth/src/__tests__/ks839-a-wildcard-allow-list-grants-nothing.test.ts`, with the ordinary header
`--- a/Blockchain/Dev/services/auth/src/__tests__/ks839-a-wildcard-allow-list-grants-nothing.test.ts` /

tamper named at the bottom into a clone of `oauth.ts` and expects the new cell RED by assertion, then expects the whole file GREEN

## What is wrong (one paragraph)

`validateScopes` (`oauth.ts:352-:355`) grants nothing when any allow-list entry, split with `parseScopeString` (`:357-:360`, the
splitter `/[\s,]+/`), yields the wildcard `*`. The token route re-splits a granted scope with that same `parseScopeString`, so the
guard is only sound while BOTH use the same splitter. JavaScript whitespace (`\s`) includes non-ASCII separators: the no-break space
U+00A0, the ideographic space U+3000, the line separator U+2028, the byte-order mark U+FEFF, and the ASCII vertical tab U+000B. The
existing cells R3 and R4 pad the wildcard only with space, tab, newline and comma. So a guard that splits with a second, narrower
tokenizer (the #1026 round-2 gate tamper G-SECOND-REGEX, `entry.split(/[ \t\n,]+/)`) keeps every existing cell green while an
allow-list entry of no-break space plus `*` mints `*` into the token again. **This task:** one new cell, R5, over five carriers
padded with those separators, asserting that each grants nothing with scope omitted, mints nothing, and grants nothing when scopes
are named; and the completeness count goes from 6 to 7. No product line changes.

## Where (no product site changes - this list is informational; every line below STAYS)

- `:353` - (correct) `  if (allowed.some(entry => parseScopeString(entry).includes('*'))) return []; // KS-839: a wildcard grants nothing, padded or not (' *', 'openid,*' split to '*' on the way to the token)` - the guard. The tamper replaces this line. Stays.
- `:359` - (correct) `  return scope.split(/[\s,]+/).filter(s => s.length > 0);` - the splitter. Stays.

The fifteen `+` lines (one in E1, fourteen in E2) are byte-exact - copy them; do not paraphrase the title or the comment, do not re-indent (2 spaces for the
`it(` line and its closing `});`, 4 spaces for the statements, 6 spaces for the carrier rows and for `.toEqual`), do not merge the
carriers into `PADDED_CARRIERS`, do not reorder them. The blank context line at the top of E1 is ONE space and nothing else. Every
other line of the file stays byte-identical. The cell reads only names declared ABOVE it in the file (`CELLS_RUN`,
`validateScopes`, `parseScopeString`, `mintedWithScopeOmitted`) or inside it (`UNICODE_CARRIERS`, `named`).

**Why `String.fromCharCode(0x...)` and not the character or a backslash escape:** four of the five separators are non-ASCII and
INVISIBLE, and a non-ASCII character in a `+` line is not reliably reproduced. A backslash-u escape in a `+` line is read back as the
character by the input JSON and by the checker, and a backslash-v is one invisible control character away from the same trap. So the
carriers are built by code point: the `+` lines are plain ASCII with no backslash, no dollar sign, no backtick and no double quote,
and at runtime `String.fromCharCode(0xa0) + '*'` is exactly the two-character string no-break space then star. Keep it that way.

Red under the tamper: R5 fails at `.toEqual` by assertion. The narrower tokenizer does not split any of the five entries, so the
guard does not fire: with scope omitted `validateScopes` grants the entry itself and `parseScopeString` then mints `*` from it (and
`openid` beside it on the last row, which a named request is also granted). Green at the tip: `parseScopeString` splits every one of
the five separators, so the guard fires and all three arms are `[]`. The six existing cells stay green on both trees (R1-R4 use exact
`*` or ASCII separators the narrower tokenizer still splits; CONTROL and CONTROL 2 hold no wildcard entry), and COMPLETENESS counts 7.
